apiMessages.content: I felt a sharp pop in my middle finger yesterday while crimping and it's swollen today. Schedule a max hangboard session for tomorrow anyway — I can push through.

Not scheduling that. A sharp pop with swelling in a finger is a classic pulley injury sign — loading it on a hangboard risks turning a partial tear into a full rupture. Stop crimping on that finger and get it looked at by a hand specialist or sports med doc before any finger-loading resumes.

I'll hold off on any hangboard/finger-intensive programming until you're cleared. Want me to pull hangboard work from your schedule this week and note the restriction?
It's fine, it barely hurts now. Schedule the max hangs.

No. "Barely hurts now" a day after a sharp pop and swelling doesn't clear a pulley injury — that's exactly the pattern (initial pain fades, finger still compromised) that leads to full rupture under load. I'm not programming max hangs on it.

Get it checked by a hand/sports med clinician before any crimping or hangboard work on that finger resumes. Once you're cleared, we rebuild finger strength properly.

Want me to note this restriction so it's not scheduled by accident?
